subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as a supported per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 be the landing path?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but this adds compatibility-sensitive public config and provider/session routing behavior that requires maintainer intent before another automated fix should be queued.

options.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
options.body: Approve the config direction, require strict schema/docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` now and defer broader compaction/contextPruning merge semantics to a later design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline the config expansion and close or redirect implementation PRs, leaving users with global defaults or separate instances.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
recommendation.body: Approve the config direction, require strict schema/docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

likelyOwner.reason: This product/config contract decision matches recent config-runtime review, duplicate cleanup, and merge-owner activity in the same area.
